# ADR conventions

How this repo keeps its decision log, shared by every code-kestrel repo. The index is [`README.md`](README.md); a new record starts from [`template.md`](template.md).

## Using the log

1. **Before planning, list the log:** `grep -H -m2 -E '^# |Status:' docs/adr/[0-9]*.md` prints each record's title
   and status. Anything the work touches: read the record. Cite the ADRs you rely on in the plan, the PR body and any critic brief. Do not re-derive a decision that
   has a record.
2. **A critic finding against an accepted record** is filed as `CHALLENGES ADR <id>: <what changed>`, not as a
   defect. A diff that makes a significant decision (list below) without a record is a finding.
3. **Re-open when the world moved.** "It did not work" is a fact about a date, a tool version and a device. When a
   record's *Revisit when* condition is met, say so and propose a superseding record. **Who re-opens:** a product,
   look or product-affecting data-model decision is Shahrum's, via dialog. A purely technical decision may be
   superseded act-then-show by a session pre-authorized for that work; the new record says so in *Deciders*.
4. **Record significant decisions in the same PR** that makes them, never as a follow-up.
5. **Keep the log current in the same PR.** When code, CLAUDE.md or a README stops matching an accepted record, fix it
   in that PR: correct the stale doc, or supersede the record and flip the old record's Status in the same commit.

## When a record is owed

A Shahrum dialog pick on architecture, product model or look · a new or retired hard constraint · a reversal · a
platform floor or ceiling · a vendor, dependency or hosting choice · a process rule with an incident behind it that
shapes code (apply-before-merge) · an option a critic argued against that was kept. **Not owed:** bug fixes,
reversible implementation detail, anything a single PR can undo without anyone noticing.

## Shape

- **Files:** `docs/adr/YYYY-MM-DD-short-imperative-title.md`: the decision date, then a kebab-case title that names
  the decision (`2026-09-24-sign-in-with-apple-only.md`, not `2026-09-24-auth.md`). Two PRs open at once cannot
  collide the way a shared counter does. Records named `NNNN-` before 2026-09-24 keep their names, and `0000` seeds a
  new log. A record's **id** is its filename without `.md`. Copy `template.md`. One decision per record; two
  decisions in one dialog are two records.
- **No index table.** The folder is the log; the command in "Using the log" lists it oldest first. `README.md` is
  the front page plus any labelled repo-specific additions.
- **Sections:** header lines *Status*, *Date*, *Deciders*, *Decided in*, *Implemented* (a merge sha or PR, else `no`; a missing line is a warning, never a failure), *Supersedes* (or *Amends*); then *Context and problem*,
  *Decision* ("We will..."), *Options considered* (the losers and why, above all the one a critic argued for),
  *Consequences* (good, bad, neutral), *Confirmation* (the behaviour, check, grep or critic line that proves it, never just a
  test file name, or "none, judgement"), *Revisit when* (the conditions, or "nothing foreseen"; never omitted).
- **Statuses:** `proposed` · `accepted` · `rejected` · `deprecated` · `superseded by <id>`. A plan doc's proposal
  is `proposed`; Shahrum's dialog pick, or the merge of the PR that carries it, makes it `accepted`.
- **Immutable once accepted**, except the Status line, supersession or amendment links, and fact corrections. Changing
  course is a new record with *Supersedes <id>*; the old one's Status flips. Overriding one clause of a record that
  otherwise stands is a new record with *Amends <id>*; the old one's Status becomes `accepted; amended by <id>`. A fact
  that was wrong when written (a name, a number, a path, a consequence that described the code wrongly) is corrected in
  place when nothing is re-decided, with a header line `Amended YYYY-MM-DD: <what changed and why>`. If the fix changes
  what was decided or why, it is an *Amends* record. Nothing is deleted; the losing reasoning is the point.
- **Length:** one screen. Design detail stays in the plan doc; the record links it.
- **Dates** are the decision's day, not the write-up's; a backfilled record says "backfilled YYYY-MM-DD".

## One home per fact

| Question | Its one home | Everything else links, never restates |
|---|---|---|
| *Why* is it this way; what lost; when does it stop holding? | `docs/adr/` | the PR description links the record and stops |
| *What shipped*, and its how-to traps? | `git log --first-parent main` (each squash commit carries its PR description; `CHANGELOG.md` is the frozen record before 2026-09-24) | a lesson that changes a rule points to the incident log or the ADR |
| *What happened*: the incident behind a rule? | the repo's incident log (`docs/HISTORY.md` or equivalent), if any | the ADR links the incident |
| *How to behave now*: the operative rule? | `CLAUDE.md` | a hard constraint cites its ADR for the why, never carries it |
| *What next*, and the board's state? | the [Fletchwork Backlog](https://github.com/orgs/Fletchwork/projects/1) board (issues); `docs/ROADMAP.md` keeps direction and milestones, `HANDOFF.md` keeps traps | a DECIDED marker is one line plus the ADR id |
| *How* we build it: design detail? | the plan doc | its decisions become ADRs; the plan keeps the detail |
| What the project is and how to set it up? | `README.md` | CLAUDE.md links setup steps rather than repeating them |
| Kestrel's private working notes? | auto-memory | never a source of truth; a decision found only there gets a record |

**When two disagree:** the ADR wins on the *why* and the *options*; git on *what shipped*; CLAUDE.md on
*what to do today*; the code on *what runs*. Fix the disagreement in one PR and say which side was stale. On the ADR
side only a Status flip, a supersession link or a new record; an accepted body is never rewritten.
